newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bullish Oslo Bourse exceeds 1,300 points.
newsitem.headline: Bullish Oslo Bourse exceeds 1,300 points.

text.p: Norwegian shares roared to a new all-time high on Tuesday, exceeding 1,300 points for the first time in lively trade.
Oslo's Total share index posted a record close of 1,300,60 points, up 0.89 percent from Monday after an intra-day peak of 1,301.31. Turnover amounted to 1.35 billion crowns.
Dealers said the rise was liquidity-driven.

Hardware distributor Santech Micro Group (SMG) was heavily traded at 128 million crowns. It finished unchanged at 19.50 crowns the day after U.S. computer distributor CHS Electronic Inc offered to buy SMG for 20.50 crowns per share.

Branded goods-based conglomerate Orkla finished 1.10 percent higher at 552.50 crowns the day after it announced a deal with PepsiCo on production, distribution and sales of Pepsi-Cola and 7UP in Sweden as of 2001.
Den norske Bank (DnB) and Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse, both of which are expected to present strong profits on Wednesday, continued to climb.
DnB rose 1.21 percent to 33.50 crowns and Christiania was up 2.52 percent at 28.70 crowns.
